name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo Loop
area: Tre Cime Nature Park · Sexten Dolomites
access: Toll road from Misurina to Rifugio Auronzo (2,320 m)
trending_reason: The most-recommended hike in the Dolomites; the north-face view of the three peaks is the region’s signature shot
blurb: A gentle loop round the three great spires via Rifugio Lavaredo, Forcella Lavaredo and Rifugio Locatelli, with WWI tunnels and the classic north-face view.

name: Seceda Ridge Viewpoint
access_note: Since July 2025 landowners have intermittently run a €5 turnstile on the path to the summit cross; a signed bypass keeps the viewpoint free.
trending_reason: The tilted Odle ridge is one of the most-shared Alpine images; summer crowds of thousands a day led to the 2025 turnstile protest
blurb: The postcard of the Dolomites: a short stroll from the cable car to the tilted Seceda ridge, with the jagged Odle spires dropping away beside you.

name: Lago di Braies Lake Circuit
access: Summer 9–16 h car closure: pre-book parking or take the shuttle bus
trending_reason: Emerald lake and wooden boathouse under the Seekofel; one of the most photographed lakes in the Alps
blurb: A flat loop round the emerald lake under the Seekofel walls, with rowing boats at the famous wooden boathouse; also the start of the Alta Via 1.

name: Lago di Sorapis
access: Car or summer bus from Cortina to Passo Tre Croci (1,809 m)
trending_reason: Milky-turquoise glacial lake on every Dolomites must-do list
blurb: A balcony path with short cabled sections and ladders to a startlingly turquoise lake below the Sorapiss walls and Rifugio Vandelli.

name: Giro delle Cinque Torri
access: 5 Torri chairlift from Bai de Dones (1,889 m), or walk up in about 1 h
trending_reason: Open-air WWI museum among five rock towers; big views for little effort
blurb: A short loop round five sheer rock towers through restored WWI trenches, with the Tofane, Marmolada and Lagazuoi all around.

name: Adolf Munkel Trail
area: Puez-Odle Nature Park · Val di Funes
access: Zans trailhead, Val di Funes (car park fills early)
trending_reason: Larch-forest balcony right under the Geisler spires, with hut lunches at Geisleralm
blurb: A balcony path through larch forest right beneath the north faces of the Odle/Geisler spires, finishing at the Gschnagenhardt and Geisler huts.

name: Lagazuoi WWI Tunnels
access: Lagazuoi cable car up from Passo Falzarego, then walk down through the tunnels
access_note: Helmet, headlamp, gloves and a via-ferrata kit are mandatory in the tunnels.
trending_reason: Headlamp descent through restored Austro-Italian war tunnels, from the famous Lagazuoi hut terrace
blurb: Ride up to Rifugio Lagazuoi, then descend inside the mountain through restored WWI tunnels by headlamp, with an optional exit along the exposed Cengia Martini ledge.
description: Ride the Lagazuoi cable car from Passo Falzarego to the hut terrace at 2,752 m, one of the great Dolomites viewpoints, then walk back down inside the mountain through the Galleria del Lagazuoi, a WWI mine tunnel dug by the Italian army under the Austrian positions. The tunnels are steep, wet and pitch-dark in places: headlamp, helmet, gloves and a via-ferrata kit are required. The exposed Cengia Martini ledge is an optional exit.

name: Alpe di Siusi Meadow Walk
start_name: Mont Sëuc cable car top station
access: Mont Sëuc cable car from Ortisei
trending_reason: Europe’s largest high-altitude pasture, framed by the Sassolungo and Sciliar
blurb: Rolling high meadows dotted with hay huts beneath the Sassolungo and Sciliar: the gentlest big view in the Dolomites.

name: Sassolungo Circuit (Friedrich-August-Weg)
access: Passo Sella (bus or drive via Selva)
trending_reason: The Langkofel group from every side; a staple of Val Gardena hiking lists
blurb: A hut-to-hut circuit on the Friedrich-August-Weg under the huge walls of the Sassolungo, with the Marmolada glacier across the valley.

name: Rifugio Nuvolau from Passo Giau
trending_reason: The oldest hut in the Dolomites on a 360° summit; a favourite sunset spot
blurb: From Passo Giau round the Ra Gusela to the summit hut of Nuvolau, the oldest in the Dolomites, with a 360° view from the Civetta to the Tofane.
description: From Passo Giau the path climbs round the Ra Gusela to Rifugio Nuvolau, a hut perched on the 2,575 m summit since 1883 and one of the oldest in the Dolomites. The 360° view takes in the Civetta, Pelmo, Tofane, Marmolada and the Cinque Torri right below. The last pull to the hut is steep but not technical; the loop back to the pass makes a full half-day.

name: Vajolet Towers & Rifugio Re Alberto
access: Vigo cable car to Ciampedìe, then 45 min on foot to Gardeccia (or chairlifts from Pera)
access_note: Rifugio Re Alberto I is open about 20 Jun – 20 Sep.
trending_reason: Alpenglow on the Vajolet spires is a classic Dolomites image
blurb: Past Rifugio Vajolet and up a short cabled gully to the hut at the foot of the three Vajolet towers, deep inside the Rosengarten.
description: From Rifugio Gardeccia the trail climbs past the Vajolet and Preuss huts, then up a steep rocky gully with fixed cables to Rifugio Re Alberto I (Gartlhütte) at 2,621 m, tucked at the foot of the three Vajolet Towers deep inside the Rosengarten. Gardeccia is about 45 minutes on foot from the Ciampedìe cable car above Vigo di Fassa, or reached by the chairlifts from Pera. The hut opens roughly late June to late September.

name: Lago di Carezza
access: Paid car parks P1/P2 with a short tunnel to the lake; bus 180
trending_reason: The “rainbow lake” mirroring the Latemar, a fixed stop on the Great Dolomites Road
blurb: A short path round a small, vivid green-blue lake that mirrors the Latemar spires: a 30-minute stop on the Great Dolomites Road.
description: A short, nearly flat path circles the Karersee, a small spring-fed lake famous for its shifting green-blue colours and the reflection of the Latemar spires. It is a 30-minute stop on the Great Dolomites Road: park at the paid P1/P2 car parks and walk through the short underpass to the shore. The lakeshore is fenced to protect it; swimming and drones are banned.

name: Santa Maddalena Viewpoint
access: Paid car parks in Santa Maddalena; no parking on Magdalenaweg or Panoramaweg
trending_reason: The church-and-Geisler-peaks view is the stock image of the Dolomites
blurb: An easy walk above the village to the classic view of Santa Maddalena church with the Geisler spires behind, and the meadow chapel of St. Johann in Ranui just down the valley.
description: The classic view of Val di Funes: a short walk up the Panoramaweg above Santa Maddalena to the viewpoint over its church with the Odle/Geisler spires behind. Carry on down the valley to St. Johann in Ranui, the little baroque chapel standing alone in a meadow beneath the same peaks. Best at sunrise or late afternoon. Use the paid car parks: parking on the narrow lanes is prohibited and drones are banned.

name: Monte Piana Open-Air Museum
access: Jeep shuttle from Misurina / Lago d’Antorno to Rifugio Bosi (road closed to cars)
trending_reason: WWI front-line trenches facing the Tre Cime; a quieter alternative to the Tre Cime loop
blurb: A plateau loop through restored WWI trenches and tunnels on the old Austro-Italian front line, with the Tre Cime and Cadini right in front of you.
description: Monte Piana was one of the fiercest fronts of WWI, with the Austrian and Italian lines running across its flat summit only metres apart. A signed open-air museum now leads through restored trenches, tunnels and gun positions, with the north faces of the Tre Cime and the Cadini di Misurina right in front of you. Reach Rifugio Bosi by the jeep shuttle from Misurina (the road is closed to cars), then loop round the plateau.

name: Alta Via 1
access: Bus or shuttle to Lago di Braies; bus home from Belluno
trending_reason: The most popular multi-day trek in the Dolomites
blurb: The classic hut-to-hut traverse from Lago di Braies to Belluno over Fanes, Lagazuoi and Nuvolau, past the Pelmo and Civetta.
description: The best-known hut-to-hut trek in the Dolomites: about 120 km from Lago di Braies to Belluno in 8–12 days. It crosses the Fanes plateau, climbs to Rifugio Lagazuoi (2,752 m, the high point), passes the Cinque Torri and Nuvolau, then the Pelmo and the Civetta walls before dropping through the wild Schiara group. No glacier crossings, a few exposed cabled passages and an optional via ferrata near the end. Book the huts months ahead for July and August.

name: Via delle Bocchette Centrali
access: On foot from the Vallesinella car park via Rifugio Brentei, or the Grostè lift
access_note: Full via-ferrata kit and helmet required. Rifugio Pedrotti reopens 20 Jun 2026 after renovation.
trending_reason: The most famous ledge via ferrata in the Alps, past the Campanile Basso
blurb: Airy ledges and ladders through the heart of the Brenta, from Rifugio Alimonta past the Campanile Basso to the Bocca di Brenta.
description: The heart of the Brenta’s famous Via delle Bocchette: airy ledges, iron ladders and cables threaded between the towers of the Brenta, past the Campanile Basso, from Rifugio Alimonta to the Bocca di Brenta and Rifugio Pedrotti. From the Vallesinella car park above Madonna di Campiglio it is a very long day (about 18 km and 1,300 m of ascent), so many split it with a hut night. Full via-ferrata kit and helmet required; early in the season the gullies can need crampons.
